title: We Must Sing Its Praises; There's An Endless Bounty Of Pleasure At Stratford's

display_heading.headline: We Must Sing Its Praises
display_heading.deck: There's An Endless Bounty Of Pleasure At Stratford's The Music Man

contact_edits.before: The Avon stage can't match the vistas of the shows previous airing at the Festival Theatre. Philosophically I approve of the decision to restrict musicals to the proscenium house, but I have to confess that The Music Man was one of two shows -- Fiddler on the Roof, also about a town, was the other -- that justified the epic look. Still, Patrick Clark's sets bring striped-suit ice-cream-parlour America to delectable life, and the population is by and large terrific. It includes such surprise musical casting as Sara Topham, doing some earnestly bedraggled hoofing, and Michelle Fisk, wonderfully warm, sharp and tuneful as the heroine's mother. Those more accustomed to this kind of thing include Eddie Glen, an expert sidekick; a formidable colla voce quartet (Laird Mackintosh, Shawn Wright, Jonathan Monro, Marcus Nance); and a malapropping Mayor (Lee MacDougall) who, like the hero he opposes, is delightful but a little short on threat. There are also some more-than-bearable children, headed by Christopher Van Hagen as the lisping boy who learns to sing Gary, Indiana. He is key to the redemptive ending, which comes a bit sudden in this production but casts a glow anyway. The Music Man beat West Side Story at the 1958 Tonys. Historians usually reckon this to be an injustice, but I'm not so sure. - The Music Man is in repertory through Nov. 1 at the Avon Theatre, Stratford. Call 1-800-567-1600 for more information.
